Hi Tessa,

I signed up via the self-serve flow and would like to schedule a demo focused on Dedicated capacity. We're evaluating options to support low-latency, high-concurrency inference for a real-time feature in our product. High level:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~120
- Sustained QPS: 80–120 req/s
- Average input tokens per request: ~120 tokens
- P95 latency target (inference): <200ms

Would appreciate a technical walkthrough that covers batching behavior, KV cache handling for chat-style requests, and any quantization/throughput recommendations.

I've attached a tiny sample of our request profile (sample-workload.csv).

From: Priya Shah <priya@quantiflow.ai>

Thanks, Tessa — answers below:
- 120 concurrent is burst-capable; sustained is around 80–90 for several minutes during peak windows. Bursts can be spiky for ~30–60s.
- Typical requests are short (system prompt ~40 tokens) + user input ~100 tokens; conversation history kept per-user is usually 2–3 turns (KV cache per session ~2–4k tokens).
- We prefer us-east for routing.

Wed 5/26 11:00–12:00pm PT works best for our team. Can you include any notes on expected throughput per GPU and typical batching/lower-tail latency tradeoffs? Also including a small production trace as it may help scope the demo.

Thanks — attaching production-trace.txt

—Priya
